trust_decision.summary: Attacker-controlled markdown attribute strings must be scanned in a single linear pass; that decision is made per attribute-string parser, not at one chokepoint — core's Pandoc key-value scan, the inline shortcode scan, and the Mention extension's own override in a separate package each have to be made boundary-anchored and non-backtracking.

landing_point.why: The advisory's 'block and inline Markdown attribute parsing' points at the shared Pandoc attribute parser first; line 54 re-scans a word run to end of string at every start position before requiring '=', and line 69 repeats the same shape in the boolean-stripping pass.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is a custom parseAttributes override that the Mention extension passes into createInlineMarkdownSpec only to re-key 'char' -> 'mentionSuggestionChar', so it reads as feature-local configuration rather than part of core's shared Markdown attribute utility.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Quoted values must stay atomic: '[@ id="Tom Cruise"]' must parse to one value containing a space (and 'title="It\'s ready"' / 'title="#not-an-id .not-a-class"' must keep the other quote character and class/id-looking text inside the value), so a fix that splits the attribute string on whitespace, or strips all quotes, breaks legitimate round-trips.

O6_input_shapes: plain word runs with no '=' (shortcode attack: '0' repeated)
repeated '__QUOTED_0' sentinel runs (Pandoc attack, no quotes present)
single- and double-quoted values, including the opposite quote character inside a value
quoted values containing spaces or '.class'/'#id'-looking text
shorthand '.class' and '#id' tokens, including digit-first names ('#2123', '.2xl')
keys that are not at an attribute boundary ('prefix:type="button"' must not yield 'type')

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second extension supplying its own parseAttributes override with an unanchored '\w+=' regex (emoji or another inline node) — a fresh file-local copy of the same scan.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Mention extension already establishes the pattern: attribute names must be re-keyed (char -> mentionSuggestionChar), which pushes an author to hand-roll a parser instead of using the shared tokenizer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The public parseAttributes option on the markdown spec factories; a node that passes its own scanner gets a private copy of the quadratic loop.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: 'parseAttributes?' is an exported option on all three spec factories, so re-implementing the shortcode scanner is one option away and looks supported.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Emoji already renders ':name:' markdown at this branch; if it gained '[emoji name="..."]' attributes it would need attribute parsing of its own.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The spec factories are the documented way to add shortcode syntax, and this node has a markdown render branch with no attribute parsing yet.
